article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Wedding Cake × Gelato 45
Breeder: The Cali Connection
THC Content: 19-22%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: beta-caryophyllene , limonene , humulene
Primary Flavors: Vanilla, chocolate, cream, coffee
Flowering Time (Indoor): 63–67 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid to late October
Indoor Yield: 200–280 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Tiramisu is one of the rare dessert-named cannabis strains whose flavor actually has a convincing relationship to the food on the label. Vanilla and creamy sweetness arrive first, but the flower does not stop at sugar. Cocoa, coffee-like bitterness, buttery richness, earth, and a touch of hash build underneath, creating something closer to a layered dessert than a one-note candy strain. The Cali Connection achieved that character by bringing together Wedding Cake and Gelato 45, two California hybrids whose shared Cookies-family ancestry reinforces resin, dense flowers, potency, and sweetness without making the finished plant taste identical to either parent.

There is a similarly layered quality to the experience. Tiramisu can open with an upbeat, sociable cerebral shift before physical relaxation gradually becomes more apparent, allowing this weed strain to occupy a comfortable space between daytime stimulation and nighttime heaviness. In the garden, it follows the same balanced theme: plants develop solid structure, respond well to topping, clone easily, and mature in roughly 63–67 days. Rather than being bred around one spectacular statistic, this cultivar succeeds through the way flavor, resin, structure, and effects fit together.
Genetics and Lineage

The Cali Connection created Tiramisu by crossing Wedding Cake with Gelato 45. Wedding Cake is the Triangle Mints #23 selection associated with Triangle Kush and Animal Mints genetics. Triangle Kush contributes classic OG-family qualities—earth, lemon, fuel, resin, and considerable potency—while Animal Mints brings Cookies influence, sweet dough, mint, and a thick coating of trichomes. Wedding Cake became popular because those elements combine into dense, aromatic marijuana with a creamy-sweet flavor that can still carry a noticeable earthy and peppery foundation.

Gelato 45 comes from the Gelato family developed from Sunset Sherbet and Thin Mint Cookies . Sunset Sherbet adds sweet fruit, cream, and a rich dessert character, while Thin Mint reinforces dough, herbs, spice, mint, and resin. Phenotype #45 became especially valued for combining vigorous structure with the unmistakably smooth, creamy aroma associated with high-quality Gelato. Bringing it into the Tiramisu cross amplifies the dessert side of Wedding Cake without eliminating its OG-derived weight and earthiness.

The pedigree contains considerable genetic overlap, and that is part of the point. Cookies and OG-related ancestry appear repeatedly through both sides rather than being paired with an unrelated landrace or long-flowering sativa. Consequently, the cultivar tends toward a coherent modern California expression: firm flowers, high resin potential, sweet cream, earth, spice, and a balanced effect. The differences between the parents provide enough contrast to introduce coffee, chocolate, vanilla, and buttery nuances, while their shared heritage helps keep plant structure and flowering behavior relatively predictable.
Effects and Experience

Tiramisu does not necessarily begin as heavily as its rich dessert profile might imply. The opening stage can feel buoyant and mentally engaging, with mood becoming lighter and conversation flowing more naturally. Some consumers find music, movies, gaming, or creative hobbies particularly enjoyable during this phase because the cerebral shift is noticeable without immediately producing the hazy mental slowdown associated with heavier indica weed. At moderate amounts, the experience can remain surprisingly social.

Relaxation gradually moves into the foreground rather than arriving all at once. Muscles begin to feel less tense, the pace of thought becomes more comfortable, and sitting down starts to sound more appealing even while the mind remains interested in whatever is happening. That progression makes this hybrid flexible enough for late afternoon or evening use. Smaller servings may preserve more energy and talkativeness, while larger ones emphasize the heavier Cookies, OG, and Gelato side of the family.

Potency depends strongly on the individual plant and finished batch. The breeder does not assign one official THC figure, while commercial examples have appeared across a broad range from the high teens upward. That variability makes the laboratory result on the actual product more useful than a universal strain number. Overconsumption can produce dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, mental fog, or temporary anxiety, and substantial doses may turn the comfortable body relaxation into pronounced drowsiness.
Medical Benefits

For medical cannabis consumers, Tiramisu may be most interesting when mental stress and physical tension occur at the same time. The brighter first portion of the experience may make repetitive thoughts or everyday pressure feel less dominant, while the developing body effect can reduce how noticeable muscular tightness or general soreness feels. This combination gives the cultivar a different niche from marijuana that is either intensely stimulating or immediately sedating.

As the session moves forward, appetite stimulation and deeper relaxation may become more noticeable. Some people may therefore prefer the strain later in the day, particularly when they want to unwind without being mentally flattened at the beginning. Stronger doses can become sleepy enough to support an evening routine, although individual reactions vary and the cultivar should not be treated as a guaranteed sleep aid. High-THC cannabis can also worsen anxiety in susceptible consumers, making dose selection important.

Commonly reported terpene profiles include beta-caryophyllene, limonene, and humulene. Caryophyllene contributes pepper, dry wood, and warm spice; limonene can brighten the sweeter flavor with citrus; and humulene adds earthy, woody depth. These compounds help shape aroma and may influence the overall cannabis experience, but they should not be interpreted as proof that the strain treats a particular medical condition. Patients should rely on the actual cannabinoid and terpene analysis of their product and consider medication interactions, tolerance, and professional medical advice where appropriate.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Tiramisu’s strongest claim to distinction is its flavor. The Cali Connection specifically describes a blend of soft vanilla and chocolate with creamy hash and a smooth buttery undertone. That description fits the cultivar better than the generic “sweet” label often attached to dessert weed. Vanilla provides the initial softness, while cocoa and coffee-like bitterness keep the sweetness from becoming cloying. Earth and hash sit beneath those brighter notes, giving the bouquet enough depth to resemble baked dessert rather than flavored candy.

Breaking open a flower can expose additional layers of dough, dry spice, mild fuel, and occasionally citrus. Gelato 45 tends to push the creamy side forward, while Wedding Cake supplies more earth, pepper, and pastry-like richness. Certain plants smell distinctly coffee-forward; others emphasize vanilla cream or chocolate. The difference is important for growers selecting keeper plants because Tiramisu offers more than one desirable interpretation of the same general dessert profile.

On the palate, sweetness often appears before the heavier flavors. Vanilla and cream can coat the tongue on the inhale, followed by cocoa, coffee, and buttery earth as the vapor or smoke expands. A hash-like finish may remain afterward along with mild spice. Lower-temperature vaporization tends to preserve the creamy and aromatic top notes most clearly, whereas combustion strengthens the toasted, earthy, and coffee-like qualities. Slow drying and an adequate cure are particularly valuable because the nuanced cream-and-vanilla portion can disappear if the harvest is dried too aggressively.
Growing Information

Tiramisu was bred as a practical plant rather than merely a flavor experiment. The Cali Connection describes the structure as solid and influenced positively by both parents, with good production and dependable cloning characteristics. Plants may naturally favor more upright growth, and the breeder specifically recommends topping when additional sideways development is desired. Done early, topping encourages a broad, robust framework with several productive branches instead of allowing one central leader to dominate the available light.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 63–67 days, or about nine to nine and a half weeks. The breeder lists an indoor yield of roughly 200–280 grams per square meter. That figure is more conservative than many exaggerated seed-industry claims and should still be treated as a reference rather than a guarantee. Light intensity, canopy coverage, plant count, vegetative time, root volume, irrigation, nutrition, and environmental stability all influence final production.

Training is useful because the plant’s structure can be manipulated into a wider canopy without requiring extreme techniques. Low-stress training after topping can separate major branches and expose additional flower sites, while a trellis provides support as the buds gain weight. Clones generally establish well, making the cultivar attractive to growers who find a particularly flavorful mother and want to repeat it. Maintaining consistent environmental conditions is more valuable than attempting to force unusually rapid growth with heavy feeding.

The flowers become increasingly resinous during the final weeks, reflecting both Wedding Cake and Gelato ancestry. That trichome coverage can make the cultivar useful for concentrates, especially when a selected phenotype carries the breeder-described vanilla, chocolate, creamy hash, and buttery flavor into rosin or sift. Resinous flowers can also become dense, so late-flower airflow deserves attention. Moderate humidity and sufficient spacing reduce the chance of moisture lingering between tightly packed calyxes.

Outdoor cultivation is possible where the season remains favorable into October. A 63–67-day flowering cycle will commonly place maturity around mid- to late October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates, although the exact date depends on latitude and when natural flowering begins. Gardens with warm, dry autumns are better suited to fully finishing the dense flowers than regions where sustained cold rain begins early.

Root space and direct sunlight can allow outdoor plants to become considerably larger than their indoor counterparts, even though the breeder does not provide a standardized outdoor yield. Early topping can build a broader framework capable of using available sunlight efficiently, while stakes or netting may be worthwhile as flowers gain weight. Growers in humid areas should keep the interior canopy open and watch mature flowers closely during wet weather. When properly finished and cured, the main reward is not just weight but preservation of the cultivar’s unusual dessert-like terpene character.
FAQ
What strains make Tiramisu?

The Cali Connection created Tiramisu by crossing Wedding Cake with Gelato 45. Wedding Cake brings Triangle Kush and Animal Mints-associated genetics, while Gelato 45 belongs to the Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint Cookies family. Both parents contribute dense flowers, heavy resin, sweetness, and substantial Cookies and OG influence.
Is Tiramisu indica or sativa?

The breeder describes Tiramisu as an indica-sativa hybrid rather than assigning a rigid percentage. Its experience also behaves in a balanced manner, often beginning uplifted, euphoric, and social before gradually becoming more physically relaxing. Dose and phenotype can push an individual harvest toward either side.
What does Tiramisu weed taste like?

Vanilla, chocolate, cream, coffee, buttery sweetness, earthy hash, and mild spice form the core profile. The Cali Connection particularly emphasizes soft vanilla and chocolate flavors with creamy hash and a smooth buttery finish, giving the strain a convincing connection to the dessert that inspired its name.
How long does Tiramisu take to flower?

The Cali Connection lists a flowering period of 63–67 days, or roughly nine to nine and a half weeks indoors. Outdoors, plants generally need enough favorable weather to mature around mid- to late October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
How much does Tiramisu yield?

The breeder lists approximately 200–280 grams per square meter indoors. Outdoor production is not standardized and depends heavily on climate, root volume, plant size, training, sunlight, and cultivation technique. Topping can help increase lateral growth and create a wider productive canopy.
Final Thoughts on Tiramisu

Tiramisu demonstrates why dessert cannabis does not need to rely on an exaggerated name or overwhelmingly sugary flavor. Wedding Cake and Gelato 45 already share enough Cookies and OG-related ancestry to produce dense resinous flowers, but their differences create the details that matter: vanilla, cocoa, coffee, cream, hash, earth, and an unusually smooth buttery finish. The completed profile feels layered rather than simply sweet.

The experience follows a similar pattern. An upbeat and social opening can make the strain feel lighter than expected, while the body slowly becomes calmer as the session develops. That transition gives Tiramisu useful flexibility, particularly during the late afternoon and evening, when a consumer may want cerebral engagement first and deeper relaxation later.

Cultivators receive a comparatively straightforward modern hybrid with a 63–67-day flowering period, solid structure, good cloning ability, and a documented indoor yield of approximately 200–280 grams per square meter. Early topping can improve lateral growth, and attentive humidity management helps protect the resinous flowers near harvest. Phenotype selection becomes especially worthwhile when searching for plants that maximize the coffee, chocolate, vanilla, or creamy-hash side of the profile.

For growers and consumers drawn to modern California dessert genetics, Tiramisu offers more substance than its name alone suggests. Its appeal comes from the way two familiar families have been combined into cannabis with a genuinely distinctive flavor progression and a balanced high. Sweet without becoming simplistic and relaxing without immediately becoming dull, it is a cultivar whose layered character fits its culinary namesake unusually well.
